name: Sisera
title: Canaanite military commander
summary: Sisera was the military commander of Jabin, the Canaanite king of Hazor, who oppressed the Israelites for twenty years. He was defeated by Barak and Deborah in a great battle at the Kishon River and was killed by Jael, who drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept.

keyEvents.title: The Oppression of Israel
keyEvents.description: Sisera was the military commander for King Jabin of Hazor and oppressed the Israelites for twenty years with his nine hundred iron chariots.

keyEvents.title: Deborah and Barak's Resistance
keyEvents.description: The prophetess Deborah called Barak to gather an army of ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun to fight against Sisera.

keyEvents.title: The Battle at the Kishon River
keyEvents.description: The Lord threw Sisera and his entire army into confusion, and Barak struck them down with the edge of the sword. Sisera jumped from his chariot and fled on foot.

keyEvents.title: Sisera's Flight
keyEvents.description: Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between King Jabin and the family of Heber.

keyEvents.title: Sisera's Death at Jael's Hand
keyEvents.description: Jael took a tent peg and a hammer, and while Sisera lay in deep sleep, she drove the peg through his temple so that he died.

keyEvents.title: The Song of Deborah and Barak
keyEvents.description: Sisera's defeat and death were celebrated in the song of Deborah and Barak, which also describes his mother's desperate waiting for his return.
